DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11808.topic: Timeliness of inpatient MDT formulation meetings
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11808.setting: Maple Ward, adult mental health inpatient ward, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11808.standard: TEWV NHS Foundation Trust standard: formulation meeting within 72 hours of admission with full MDT participation

cycle1.result: 27% of cases met the 72-hour standard; mean interval admission to formulation 4.9 days (median 4; range 1–10 days).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11808.other_findings: Psychologists (13%) and occupational therapists (25%) attended infrequently and carers were present in 46%; documentation gaps included missing capacity assessment (91%), legal status (55%) and clinical impression (49%). Recommendations included scheduling triggers, protected daily slots and a standard documentation template.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.010.standard: Royal College of Ophthalmologists 2018 guidelines on hydroxychloroquine dosing and retinopathy screening

cycle1.dates: Patients starting HCQ April 2013 to November 2014, followed to 30 November 2019; screening 1 November 2018 to 30 June 2019
cycle1.result: Of 86 eligible patients, 23% were prescribed a dose of >5mg/kg/day; 10% had eGFR <60; none on tamoxifen. 29 patients attended screening and none had HCQ retinopathy.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.010.other_findings: Of 207 patients who started HCQ, 43% remained on the drug at 5 years. A disproportionately high number of 'lost referrals' was being investigated, possibly due to IT issues or the paused screening service.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10627.topic: Physical health assessment in alcohol use disorder
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10627.standard: Recent blood tests, FIB-4 scoring and FibroScan for clients with alcohol use disorder

cycle1.result: 175 (87.5%) had recent blood tests; 134 (67%) had all components to calculate FIB-4; 90 (40%) had undergone FibroScan.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10627.intervention: Targeted clinician training, updated blood test request protocols to include all FIB-4 components, and revised guidelines to reoffer FibroScan to clients with abnormal liver function tests.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10627.other_findings: AST was not routinely measured unless specifically requested, which not all staff knew. A follow-up audit was planned in six months.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11849.setting: NHS Borders Mental Health for Older Adults Service memory assessment clinic
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11849.standard: All patients with suspected dementia should have a documented decision and rationale about neuroimaging, and the majority should be imaged unless clinical justification is recorded (NICE and SIGN guidance)

cycle1.result: Documented consideration of neuroimaging 59%; neuroimaging performed in 18%.

cycle2.dates: Referrals January to March 2024; reviewed February to August 2025
cycle2.result: Documented consideration of neuroimaging in 45 patients (88.2%); neuroimaging performed in 27 patients (53%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11849.other_findings: Of the 24 not imaged, eight (33%) had neuroimaging in the preceding two years; the commonest rationale for not imaging was that the diagnosis was already clear.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.099.standard: Consent documentation and governance standards for clinical photography (General Data Protection Regulation)

cycle1.result: Documented consent present in 75 of 200 (37.5%); 125 of 200 (62.5%) had no documented consent. Of documented consent, 55 of 75 (73%) on consent forms and 20 of 75 (27%) in clinical notes.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.099.intervention: Development of CliniSnap, a secure digital photography workflow with patient identifier verification, in-app consent confirmation, no camera-roll storage and direct upload to the electronic record.
DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.099.other_findings: Eleven of 211 image sets (5.2%) could not be matched to a patient encounter, highlighting traceability risks. Pilot and re-audit were planned.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.418.setting: North West based primary care practice
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.418.standard: NICE: patients aged 18–25 started on antidepressants reviewed at 1 week; all others within 2 weeks

cycle1.result: Aged 18–25: median first follow-up 3 weeks, 8% compliance. Aged >25: median 4 weeks, 19% compliance.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.418.other_findings: 58% had a mental health practitioner appointment mentioning medication within 4 weeks. A practice meeting, an MHP medication pro-forma and a re-audit in 6 months were planned.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.409.setting: Inpatient forensic and rehabilitation psychiatry services, NHS Ayrshire & Arran
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.409.standard: Scottish Government 2017 National Standard for Monitoring the Physical Health of People Being Treated with Clozapine

cycle1.result: Fasting glucose in 10/18 and lipid profile in 12/18 in preceding 6 months; LFTs in 18/18 in last year; BMI, heart rate and blood pressure documented in all; ECG in 12/18 in last year.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.409.intervention: Physical health monitoring checklist planned for forensic wards.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.409.other_findings: The rehabilitation ward, which already used a monitoring checklist, achieved 100% adherence. Re-audit was planned in 6 months.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.050.setting: Eight hospitals, emergency general surgery admissions (Irish Surgical Research Collaborative)

cycle1.result: 52% were frail (135/269); frailty was associated with more complications (p<0.001), longer stay (p=0.002) and higher one-year mortality (20% vs 8%, p=0.006). Only 16% of frail patients were seen by a geriatrician (20/122).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.050.other_findings: Of 21 laparotomies, one patient was seen by a geriatrician.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.838.setting: 19 of 39 inpatient and outpatient psychiatric units across North Wales
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.838.standard: Public Health England guidance on personal protective equipment

cycle1.result: About 50% of staff donned PPE as per guidance (Central 85%, West 22%); only 21% doffed as per guidance.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.838.intervention: Planned designated donning and doffing areas, staff teaching sessions and reminders.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.838.other_findings: There were no designated donning and doffing areas in outpatient units, and staff often did not wear masks within 2 metres of other staff.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.126.setting: Seven CAMHS teams, south region of Derbyshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.126.standard: Locally agreed protocol for recording medication history in the specified section of PARIS

cycle1.result: 13% had medication recorded in the correct section of PARIS.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.126.intervention: Teaching delivered to teams following the 2017 audit.

cycle2.result: 74% (n = 58) had medication recorded in the correct section of PARIS; of these, 86% had drug names correct, 79% correct dose, 71% correct frequency and 81% regular/PRN recorded.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.126.other_findings: Compliance varied between teams from 0% to 100%. Further teaching was delivered and a move to combined documentation and e-prescribing (SystmOne) was supported.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.573.topic: Physical observations documentation and NEWS escalation
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.573.setting: Mental health services for older people (MHSOP) inpatient wards
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.573.standard: Local and national guidance on recording physical (NEWS) and psychiatric observations

cycle1.result: Paper documentation: NEWS scores correctly documented 87%; raised NEWS scores escalated and reviewed 0%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.573.intervention: Introduction of Nervecentre electronic observation recording, which prompts when observations are due, calculates scores and allows direct escalation.

cycle2.result: NEWS scores correctly documented 100%; raised NEWS scores escalated to a senior and reviewed 80%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.573.other_findings: Improvement was seen in almost all physical observation domains, but psychiatric observations (still on paper) did not meet local or national guidance.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11833.topic: Dementia referral pathway in intellectual disability
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11833.setting: East and West Kent Mental Health of Learning Disability (MHLD) teams, Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11833.standard: NICE NG54: refer people with learning disabilities and suspected dementia to a specialist psychiatrist

cycle1.result: 48% of dementia-related referrals accepted (82% East vs 25% West); psychiatric input in 84%; 77% redirected to MAS or CLDT; no confirmed diagnoses at initial or three-month follow-up.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11833.other_findings: In a staff survey (n=18), 83% supported a formalised pathway and confidence gaps in diagnosis and prescribing were reported. 59% of referrals had Down's syndrome.

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.11.013.topic: Sliding hip screw versus intramedullary nail outcomes
DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.11.013.setting: Scottish hospitals, Scottish Hip Fracture Audit data

cycle1.result: 9867 (72%) received SHS. No difference in 30 or 60-day survival; IMN had lower early mobilisation (OR 0.64, 95%CI 0.59–0.70; p<0.001) and lower discharge to domicile by day 30 (OR 0.77, 95%CI 0.71–0.84; p<0.001). Acute and overall LOS lower for SHS (11 vs 12 and 20 vs 24 days; p<0.001).

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.11.013.other_findings: Findings were similar in a subgroup of 559 AO A1/A2 fractures; LOS differences potentially increase cost by £1230 per patient with IMN.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znaf092.047.setting: National Swiss federal statistics office (BFS) database

cycle1.result: Proportion operated in smaller hospitals fell from 38% to less than 20%; large cantonal hospitals rose from 50% to 71%. Only three centres performed a median of more than 100 resections per year.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znaf092.047.other_findings: 6.7% of resections were in patients under 50, a 30% absolute increase over the period, with a late trend towards robotic access.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.211.topic: Staff life support training on psychiatric wards
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.211.setting: Three acute inpatient psychiatric wards, Stepping Hill Hospital, Stockport
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.211.standard: NICE Clinical Guideline 25 (2005) and NPSA Rapid Response Report 2008/RRR010 on staff ability to respond to medical emergencies

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: Nursing staff training met standards except for staff new to the wards or returning from prolonged leave; gaps found for other staff groups and for the remaining standards.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.211.other_findings: Gaps were attributed mainly to new or bank staff covering wards without training or orientation to equipment and policies.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.464.setting: Wards of Wrexham Maelor Hospital, general hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.464.standard: Health board policy NU16 for alcohol withdrawal syndrome management, based on NICE guidelines

cycle1.result: Complete drinking history 4%; physical examination 84%; Wernicke's signs documented 20%; CIWA-Ar applied 44%, correctly scored 24%; benzodiazepines prescribed 38%; oral thiamine 58%; alcohol liaison opinion 16%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.464.intervention: Training programmes on alcohol withdrawal management by the alcohol liaison team for all clinical staff.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.464.other_findings: Laboratory investigation compliance ranged from 16% for GGT to 84% for full blood count; 42% had IV Pabrinex two pairs three times daily.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz103.150.setting: Two inpatient rehabilitation wards and one Day Hospital, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz103.150.standard: International and European clinical practice guidelines on sarcopenia (screening, strength assessment, muscle quantity, physical performance measures, progressive resistance training and protein-rich diet)

cycle1.result: 0% screened with a validated tool; validated strength assessment 83.3% (15) DH and 33.3% (4) inpatients; 0% muscle quantity analysis; PPMs 66.6% DH and 33.3% inpatients; PRT prescribed 94% DH and 50% inpatients.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz103.150.intervention: A multidisciplinary sarcopenia management pathway being implemented.
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz103.150.other_findings: Referral for nutritional assessment was 16.6% in DH and 75% of inpatients; all nine patients seen by clinical nutrition received a high-protein/high-calorie diet. Re-audit was planned.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab429.040.setting: International multicentre Oesophago-Gastric Anastomosis Audit (OGAA) cohort

cycle1.result: AL/CN rates 19.3% handsewn, 14.0% linear stapled, 12.1% circular stapled (p<0.001); OR 0.63 (95% CI 0.46–0.86) for circular stapled vs handsewn.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab429.040.other_findings: The effect was mainly in neck anastomoses (23.2% vs 14.6% vs 5.9%); chest anastomosis failure rates were similar across techniques.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11362.topic: Mental health liaison one-hour response breach documentation
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11362.setting: Mental Health Liaison Team, A&E of a medium-sized district general hospital, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11362.standard: Core-24 one-hour response target with documented reasons for breaches

cycle1.result: 32 of 97 referrals breached the one-hour target (33%); 10 recorded a breach reason (30%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11362.intervention: Team agreed breach codes; the A&E assessment proforma was amended and emailed to all staff, with posters in the office as reminders.

cycle2.result: 20 of 44 referrals breached (45.5%); 9 recorded reasons (45%): staffing 6 (67%), multiple referrals 1 (11%), patient left 1 (11%), other 1 (11%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11362.other_findings: Documentation remained low; 50% fewer referrals were accepted during the re-audit, possibly due to the Christmas period.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.283.topic: Absent without leave management in inpatient psychiatry
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.283.setting: Nile ward, 14-bed male psychiatric intensive care unit
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.283.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists' Quality Network for PICUs standards on leave planning, AWOL actions and carer involvement (eight criteria)

cycle1.result: All cases met six of eight criteria; carer involvement in 5 of 6; no patient had documented provision of crisis numbers before leave.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.283.other_findings: Possible AWOL risk factors were disagreement between patient and team on the care plan and concerns about mental state. A QI intervention on crisis cards was planned.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11672.setting: Bryngofal ward, adult general psychiatry inpatient ward, Hywel Dda Health Board
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11672.standard: Cycle 1: NICE review within 7 days for all and within 48 hours if at risk of suicide; cycle 2: RCPsych core standard of review within 3 days for all

cycle1.result: 42 of 44 (95%) followed up within NICE-recommended timeframes.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11672.intervention: Staff education, reinforcement of discharge risk documentation and clarification of local follow-up standards (adoption of the 3-day RCPsych standard).
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11672.other_findings: Cycle 1 non-compliance related to transfer of care to another health board and incomplete discharge risk documentation; the single cycle 2 delay was due to a ward–community communication lapse.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.412.standard: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines 14th edition and Synnovis guidance: clozapine level taken 12 hours post dose

cycle1.result: Samples >15 hours post dose: OD 56.3% (31/55), BD pm evening/night 25% (3/12), TDS 16.7% (2/12), BD am/nocte 12.9% (9/62). Samples >12 hours: OD 63.6%, BD am/nocte 51.6%, BD pm 75%, TDS 41.7%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.412.intervention: Planned: informing teams of recent samples >15 hours post dose, service education and guideline change with pharmacy support.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.412.other_findings: Timing inaccuracy was greatest with bespoke regimes; Maudsley guidance does not address bespoke dose timings. Re-audit planned in 12 months.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10681.topic: Blood test requesting in mental health services
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10681.setting: Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team North East Kent
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10681.standard: Trust protocol for requesting blood tests, with documented clinical indication when deviating

cycle1.result: Trust policy not followed in 33.3% of cases, mostly TFT, folate and B12 requested without documented indication.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10681.intervention: Trust policy poster made accessible in clinical areas, prescriber awareness of the policy, and documentation of indication when deviating from policy.

cycle2.result: Only 13.3% of cases did not follow the policy; documentation of rationale improved.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10681.other_findings: Deviation from policy remained mostly requests for TFT, B12 and folate, though less frequent.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11809.topic: Mental Health Tribunal report quality and timeliness
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11809.setting: The Cove CAMHS inpatient unit, Lancaster and South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11809.standard: 27 mandatory standards from the Mental Health Act Code of Practice, including timely report submission

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 94.4%; timely submission 64.3%; documented patient discussions 28.6%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11809.intervention: New administrative tracking system for legal deadlines and a clearer clinical pathway for recording patient discussions.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 97.1%; timely submission 100%; documented patient discussions 64.3%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11809.other_findings: 28 reports were reviewed across both years. A new digital template lacking prompts was linked to a compliance dip (85.2%), with omission of patient strengths and detention justifications.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae139.027.standard: National guidance on advance care planning

cycle1.result: Preferred place of death documented 24%; treatment escalation plan 41%; preferred place of care 59%; CPR recommendations most discussed.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae139.027.intervention: New ACP toolkit, training programme and electronic ACP flowsheet in the patient record system, via PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Preferred place of death 60% (p 0.011); treatment escalation plan 75% (p 0.014); preferred place of care 71% (p 0.066).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae139.027.other_findings: Spiritual needs, information needs, prognostic discussion, broader social needs and what mattered most to the patient did not improve significantly.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11660.setting: On-call rooms, psychiatric services in Aneurin Bevan and Cwm Taf Morgannwg health boards and Elysium Healthcare, Wales

cycle1.result: On-call rooms frequently unclean, insect-infested, lacking bed linen and used as day offices. 626.3 miles driven in total, 247.4 miles home after on-call; doctors unsure or unable to drive home safely after 20 of 38 shifts.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11660.other_findings: Doctors reported feeling frequently tired on 17 shifts and very frequently tired on 15 shifts when driving; kitchens lacked water access and lighting was poor.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa111.001.setting: University Hospital Southampton patients managed in primary care
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa111.001.standard: Guidance recommending transition to an alternative osteoporosis therapy when denosumab is stopped, and pre-injection calcium and renal function checks

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: 19 (38%) had died. Of 15 no longer on denosumab, 9 (60%) had no alternative bone protection and 3 (20%) were on alternative therapy. Of 16 still on denosumab, 13 (81%) had pre-injection calcium and 12 (75%) renal function checks.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa111.001.other_findings: Findings suggest inappropriate widespread discontinuation of denosumab without follow-on therapy, so targeted education of primary care physicians was recommended.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2022-002006.topic: Usability of audit and feedback reports
DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2022-002006.setting: General practitioners receiving the insurers' Primary Care Practice Report

cycle1.result: Qualitative study: GPs found the report poorly usable (not clinically meaningful, not recent, individual or reliable, unclear comparators and visuals) and were minimally motivated to change.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2022-002006.other_findings: GPs said well-designed feedback could motivate improvement but they receive many audit and feedback reports they hardly use.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa759.standard: BSR 2018 guideline for management of adults with SLE, NICE technology appraisal for belimumab and NHS England commissioning policy for rituximab

cycle1.dates: Any 4-week period between February and June 2018
cycle1.result: 1021 episodes of care audited; low documented compliance (<60% of visits) for formal disease-activity assessment, reduction of drug toxicity and protection against comorbidities; prednisolone recorded in 497 (49%) visits, including 28.5% of visits with inactive disease.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa759.other_findings: Dedicated clinics had better urine protein quantification (85.1% vs 78.1%) and specialised centres better BILAG Biologics Register recruitment (89.4% vs 44.4%) and blood pressure recording (95.3% vs 84.1%). 286 (28.5%) had active disease.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.602.setting: General adult psychiatry wards 1, 2 and 3, Mental Health Unit, Forth Valley Royal Hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.602.standard: NICE 2016 guidance and local discharge policy: follow-up within 7 days of discharge

cycle1.result: 26 of 41 (64%) followed up within 7 days.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.602.intervention: New discharge policy (April 2019), a 'Discharge Pause' sticker later made an electronic form, reminders to community mental health teams and a flowchart on who provides follow-up.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.602.other_findings: An interim audit in May 2019 found 39 of 46 (84%) followed up within 7 days.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad104.017.topic: Delirium screening in older surgical patients
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad104.017.setting: Surgical Assessment Unit, University Hospitals of Derby and Burton
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad104.017.standard: 4AT delirium screening of patients aged over 65 on arrival and at 48 hours

cycle1.result: 36% likely to have delirium on 4AT; 5% coded as delirium and 19% had delirium documented in notes; average 4AT completion 40%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad104.017.intervention: PDSA cycles introducing 4AT and delirium sections in care plans, plus teaching and supporting materials around the PINCHME acronym for SAU staff.

cycle2.result: Average 4AT completion rose from 40% to 64%, reaching 100% after interventions but falling back between them.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad104.017.other_findings: Staff knowledge scores improved from 43% to 92% after teaching; length of stay was 10 days with delirium vs 5.3 days without. Improvements were not sustained and delirium champions were being explored.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.455.setting: Early Intervention Service first episode psychosis team
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.455.standard: NICE guidelines on yearly physical health monitoring for patients on antipsychotics (BMI, BP, ECG, bloods, alcohol and smoking status); target 100%

cycle1.result: BMI recorded 91.67% (33); blood pressure 86.11% (31); substance use recorded 97.22% (35); ECG not recorded in 72.22% (26); full bloods up to date 75% (27); QRISK not collected in 22.73% (5/22) of eligible.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.455.intervention: Planned presentation to team and physical health check clinics.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.455.other_findings: Of 14 overweight or obese patients, 85.71% (12) received diet or exercise advice. Re-audit was planned at 3 months.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10541.standard: BCUHB guidelines for physical health monitoring of adults prescribed antipsychotic therapy

cycle1.result: Waist circumference was not measured on patients in the previous audit.

cycle2.result: Waist circumference measured in 17 of 18; HbA1c showed 6 of 18 diabetic.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10541.other_findings: By waist circumference 13 of 17 were obese and 3 overweight; by weight 11 obese, 4 severely obese and 1 overweight.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaa075.topic: Emergency laparotomy outcomes in older patients
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaa075.setting: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) hospitals in England and Wales

cycle1.result: Patients ≥65 had higher 30-day (15.3 vs 4.9%) and 90-day mortality (20.4 vs 7.2%), longer LOS and more discharge to care homes (6.7 vs 1.9%); post-operative geriatrician review increased from 8.5 to 16.5%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaa075.other_findings: Post-operative geriatrician review was associated with lower 30-day mortality (OR 0.38, CI 0.35–0.42) and 90-day mortality (OR 0.6, CI 0.56–0.65).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10696.setting: Functional old age psychiatry Wards 3 and 4, The Mount, Leeds
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10696.standard: Discharge summary completed within 7 days of discharge

cycle1.result: Ward 3: 0 of 11 completed within 7 days; Ward 4: 23% of 13 met the target.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10696.intervention: Proposed dedicated 4-hour weekly slot for junior doctors, assigning a responsible doctor at discharge and a quiet onsite workspace.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10696.other_findings: Nine barriers were identified; lack of uninterrupted time and delayed doctor allocation were prioritised. The target was extended to 14 days.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10543.setting: Memory clinic, Watermill resource centre, Berrywood Hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10543.standard: GMC guidance on fitness to drive and DVLA reporting, and Driving with Dementia or Mild Cognitive Impairment Consensus Guidelines

cycle1.result: Informed to report to DVLA 73%; informed to report to insurer 45%.

cycle2.result: Informed to report to DVLA 80% (4 of 5 drivers); informed to report to insurer 0% overall (1 of 5 drivers, 20%). Risk assessment recorded in 34 of 40.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10543.other_findings: No documentation of advice on the consequences of not reporting; 3 patients were referred to occupational therapy for driving assessment. Use of a standard template was recommended.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10576.setting: Psychiatry ward, Allied Hospital 2, Faisalabad, tertiary care hospital

cycle1.result: 156 charts with 624 prescriptions showed severe discrepancies, including missing dose, frequency, strength and start/end dates.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10576.intervention: Faculty-led workshop and mandatory teaching sessions for residents on prescription documentation.

cycle2.dates: About three months later (dates not reported)
cycle2.result: 200 charts with 650 prescriptions showed much improvement in all highlighted areas (figures not reported).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.466.topic: Management of missed appointments in community mental health
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.466.setting: West Essex community mental health teams
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.466.standard: Trust policy on non-attendance (DNA) and disengagement

cycle1.result: 98.1% notified adequately with letters to patient and GP; risk assessment completed in 50.9%; risk assessment updated in 25%; contingency plan reviewed for 26 patients; family contacted for 3.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.466.other_findings: Police/welfare checks were done for 4 patients and 31 were discharged after not responding. Risk assessment updates, crisis plan review and welfare checks fell short of policy.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.264.setting: Mid Essex ECT clinic, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Legal status documented 5%; written consent/Form 5 95%; Mini-ACE 5%; MADRS 0%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.264.intervention: Checklists and assessments introduced after an earlier QIP, then ECT discharge summaries generated for every patient from November 2021.

cycle2.result: Legal status, written consent/Form 5, Mini-ACE and MADRS all 100% (excluding patients who did not complete treatment).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.264.other_findings: Discharge summaries improved communication with referring clinicians and patient and carer satisfaction.

DOI:10.1136/leader-2025-001228.topic: Carbon footprint of shoulder dislocation pathways
DOI:10.1136/leader-2025-001228.setting: Emergency department of a major trauma centre

cycle1.result: 13 actions identified with potential saving of 86.4 kgCO2e per patient; estimated 2666 tonnes CO2e across England for 2022/2023.

DOI:10.1136/leader-2025-001228.other_findings: Traumatic dislocation without fracture made up 68.2%; 59.7% were aged 15–34 and 70.8% were male.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2020-001120.setting: Tertiary paediatric hospital, paediatric and surgical teams, Sydney Children's Hospital Randwick
DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2020-001120.standard: Evidence-based guideline for timely intravenous-to-oral antibiotic switch within 24 hours of eligibility

cycle1.dates: Baseline, before guideline launch (dates not reported)
cycle1.result: 32/50 (64%) switched within 24 hours of eligibility; median time to switch 15 hours 42 min.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2020-001120.intervention: Guideline launch with team-based education, audit and feedback.

cycle2.dates: Post-implementation within a 12-month project (dates not reported)
cycle2.result: 203/249 (82%) switched within 24 hours (p=0.006); median time to switch 4 hours 20 min (p=0.0006).

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2020-001120.other_findings: Median hospital stay fell by 14 hours (p=0.008); readmission and restarting IV therapy did not change significantly.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.272.standard: NICE: lipids at baseline, 3 months after starting a new antipsychotic, then annually; lifestyle advice and QRISK3 assessment

cycle1.result: 36 of 39 (92%) had lipids checked in last 12 months; 21 of 39 (54%) had cholesterol over 5.0; 9 of 39 (23%) had documented lifestyle discussion; 0 of 39 (0%) had QRISK3 assessment.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.272.intervention: Planned presentation to the CMHT and teaching on lifestyle advice and QRISK3.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.272.other_findings: 17 of 56 clozapine patients were excluded as already on cholesterol-lowering medication.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2023-002480.setting: Non-critical care internal medicine resident wards, DHR Health, Edinburg, Texas
DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2023-002480.standard: Inpatient hyperglycaemia guidelines; aim to reduce glucose values above 180 mg/dL by 30%

cycle1.result: 25.1% of glucose values were above 180 mg/dL.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2023-002480.intervention: Three PDSA cycles of resident education plus a pharmacy and resident audit and feedback process.

cycle2.result: 23.0% of glucose values above 180 mg/dL (p<0.05); 1045 audits of 16 095 accu-checks, mostly compliant with guidelines.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2023-002480.other_findings: The 30% reduction aim was not met, suggesting prescribing behaviour was not the key driver of hyperglycaemia; the intervention was well accepted by residents.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.479.setting: Springs Centre, 17-bed male locked secure rehabilitation ward for autism and learning disability
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.479.standard: NICE guideline recommendations on monitoring metabolic side effects of antipsychotics

cycle1.result: Blood pressure, BMI and HbA1c recorded in 100%; lipid profile 86.6%; waist circumference 60%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.479.other_findings: 79% had excess central adiposity, about 40% were obese and 20% of males had type 2 diabetes and smoked.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.371.setting: Two mental health inpatient wards (one male, one female)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.371.standard: Local and national clinical coding guidelines

cycle1.result: 5 (25%) had coding completed during admission; 1 of 4 (25%) updated after diagnosis change; 3 of 9 (33%) physical health diagnoses coded; 16 (89%) coded on last discharge.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.371.intervention: Doctors informed about clinical coding, how to access the form and its importance through teaching sessions and doctor communication groups.

cycle2.result: 10 (50%) had coding completed during admission; 3 of 4 (75%) updated after diagnosis change; 2 of 7 (29%) physical health conditions coded; 12 (75%) coded on last discharge.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.371.other_findings: Physical health coding remained poor; posters and regular reminders were suggested.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/kead484.topic: Work impact of early inflammatory arthritis

cycle1.result: 5999 (47%) in paid work ≥20 hours/week; of 2793 WPAI completers at diagnosis, 200 (7.2%) had stopped work and 344 (12.3%) changed jobs; absenteeism 30% and presenteeism 40%.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/kead484.other_findings: During follow-up 9.4% stopped work and 14.6% changed roles, with work drop-out almost entirely among routine (manual) occupations.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.468.topic: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.468.setting: Old age psychiatric inpatient unit, Wrexham, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.468.standard: Local Health Board acute inpatient admission policy: clerking and physical examination within 12 hours, bloods and medication chart within 2 hours, ECG at admission

cycle1.result: Clerking within 12 hours 67%; physical examination 52%; bloods within 2 hours 24%; ECG at admission 14%; medication chart within 2 hours 90%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.468.other_findings: Barriers included patient agitation, poor inter-team communication, no online handover system and junior doctor workload; recommendations included handover, training nurses and HCAs in phlebotomy and ECG, and ward-based doctor cover.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10536.setting: Psychiatric inpatient wards using EPMA in an NHS trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10536.standard: Trust guidelines on safe deprescribing (name and row crossed, ID, reason code, stop date)

cycle1.result: Less than 33.88% of deprescribed medications met the standards on paper Kardex.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10536.intervention: Transition from paper Kardex to an electronic prescribing and medicines administration (EPMA) system.

cycle2.result: 100% compliance with the previously measured standards; reason stated for 'other' option in 94.5%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab219.235.setting: Irish university teaching hospital, University Hospital Limerick
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab219.235.standard: Irish Heart Foundation Council for Stroke 2015: alteplase 0.9 mg/kg up to 90 mg

cycle1.result: Weights available in 92/107; 21% (19/92) received the correct 0.9 mg/kg dose, 54% (50/92) within ±10%, 25% outside ±10% (11% under- and 14% over-thrombolysed).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab219.235.other_findings: 17/92 had intracranial haemorrhage, of whom 35% (6/17) had received a dose >10% higher. Weight was not documented in 15 (9 by omission).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae175.049.setting: European Pediatric Surgical Audit (EPSA) Delphi panel, 59 hospitals in 17 countries

cycle1.result: Delphi of 96 professionals and 8 patient representatives (response rate 73%) agreed a core set of 11 baseline characteristics, 5 outcome, 2 structure and 7 process indicators.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae175.049.other_findings: Six indicators were universally prioritised; the indicators are to be implemented in EPSA.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.571.standard: Rapid tranquillisation protocol for psychiatric emergencies (stepwise de-escalation, oral then IM medication, post-administration monitoring)

cycle1.result: Only 60% adhered to recommended protocol steps; 68% bypassed oral medication or de-escalation; vital sign monitoring after administration not recorded in 30%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.571.other_findings: 12% needed a second injection, with the interval undocumented in 15% of these; medication unavailability affected 8% of aggressive cases, and ECG before haloperidol was omitted.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.406.setting: Working-age adult outpatients, 8 sector teams, Dudley mental health services
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.406.standard: NICE CG185; locally agreed 3-monthly lithium levels, 6-monthly U&Es and TFTs, and lithium results reviewed and documented at every outpatient review

cycle1.result: 3-monthly lithium monitoring 10%; 4 or more lithium tests in 12 months 17.5%; mean 2.67 tests per patient; results documented at clinic review 67.5%.

cycle2.result: 3-monthly lithium monitoring 17.5%; 4 or more tests 32.5%; mean 3.3 tests per patient; results documented at clinic review 62.5%; U&Es 6-monthly 90%; TFTs 6-monthly 85%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.406.other_findings: A lithium blood monitoring clinic was proposed to improve compliance.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab030.12.topic: Cervical spine imaging in older head injury
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab030.12.setting: Emergency Department, Stoke Mandeville Hospital, district general hospital
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab030.12.standard: Trust guidelines based on the Canadian Cervical Spine Rule for c-spine imaging in patients over 65

cycle1.result: 16% had CT c-spine in addition to CT head; c-spine examination documented in 16% of those without CT c-spine.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab030.12.intervention: Results presented at an ED education meeting and posters of CT c-spine indications displayed around the ED.

cycle2.result: 38% had CT c-spine; documented c-spine examination in those not imaged remained 16%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab030.12.other_findings: An older person's trauma team with age-appropriate triage was proposed.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.420.topic: Young onset dementia assessment and support
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.420.setting: Shepway Community Mental Health Service for Older People
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.420.standard: NICE dementia guidelines and Royal College of Psychiatrists recommendations for young onset dementia service provision

cycle1.dates: Patients open within the last 2 years (dates not reported)
cycle1.result: Mood considered in all; young onset bloods when indicated 89%; physical examination 43%; all had imaging; named practitioner in half; cognitive stimulation therapy and post-diagnostic support offered to 79%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.420.other_findings: There was no named lead for young onset dementia; referral to diagnosis took 6 months for Down syndrome dementia and 5.5 months for other types.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.265.topic: Physical health information in psychiatric discharge letters
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.265.setting: Male and female inpatient wards, Foss Park Hospital, York
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.265.standard: 100% of Lester Tool data (smoking status, BMI, ECG, blood pressure, blood results) included in discharge documents

cycle1.result: No discharge had 100% compliance; on average 23% of Lester Tool information included; no cholesterol ratios recorded; BMI 50%; smoking status 27%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.265.other_findings: 40% of female ward and 15% of male ward discharges had none of the data recorded.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.423.standard: NICE: baseline height, weight, pulse, blood pressure and cardiovascular assessment before stimulant treatment, then 6-monthly weight, blood pressure and pulse

cycle1.result: Baseline blood pressure 57% (19); pulse 39% (13); weight 51% (17); cardiovascular assessment 6% (2). At 6-month follow-up (10 patients), 0% had blood pressure, pulse or weight documented.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.423.intervention: New proforma for baseline and 6-monthly physical health monitoring to be placed in case notes; results presented at CMHT meeting.

DOI:10.1136/thorax-2026-225015.topic: Pulmonary rehabilitation enrolment and completion inequalities
DOI:10.1136/thorax-2026-225015.setting: National Respiratory Audit Programme pulmonary rehabilitation services, England and Wales

cycle1.result: 72 085 (82%) enrolled and 52 669 (60%) completed; lower odds of enrolment and completion with age <60, female gender, MRC 5 and most deprived IMD quintile.

DOI:10.1136/thorax-2026-225015.other_findings: Black ethnicity had higher odds of enrolment (OR 2.16) and completion (OR 1.50) than White ethnicity.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.094.setting: General surgery department, University Hospital Hairmyres
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.094.standard: RCSEng guidelines on operation note content

cycle1.result: not reported

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.094.intervention: Departmental education presentation and posters in theatres as reminders.

cycle2.result: Improved documentation of elective/emergency, time, anaesthesia type, indication, position, findings, tissue removed, blood loss, antibiotics and DVT prophylaxis; figures not reported in the abstract.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.094.other_findings: Documentation of date, assistant name, incision, closure and signature worsened; 193 of 239 notes were handwritten. Extra headings on the op-note and digital operation notes were suggested.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10618.topic: Memantine prescribing and renal function checks
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10618.setting: Old age psychiatry outpatient clinic, Ribchester Centre, Bury
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10618.standard: NICE guidelines on memantine indications and renal function review before prescribing

cycle1.result: Only 3 of 12 memantine prescriptions had a NICE diagnostic indication documented; all had eGFR and renal function documented in GM records, but 7 did not have these in clinic correspondence.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10618.other_findings: 395 dementia patients were screened; memantine was used as adjunct in two cases and for severe Alzheimer's disease in one.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.028.topic: Withholding antihypertensives after hip fracture surgery
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.028.setting: Orthogeriatric ward, Lister Hospital, East and North Hertfordshire NHS Trust
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.028.standard: Pre-emptive holding of ACE inhibitors and calcium channel blockers for 48 hours after neck of femur fracture surgery

cycle1.result: Antihypertensives appropriately held in 40% of cases; mean days with severe hypotension 0.62.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.028.intervention: Induction teaching for resident doctors and a revised post-operative proforma prompting holding of ACE inhibitors and CCBs.

cycle2.result: Antihypertensives appropriately held in 88% (p = 0.04); mean days with severe hypotension 0.28 (p = 0.03); hypotension incidence fell from 35% to 28% (p = 0.01).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.028.other_findings: 75% were on at least one antihypertensive on admission; in cycle 1, holding was associated with fewer days of severe hypotension (0.36 vs 0.64, p = 0.03).
